derivation:
exact (hA.orthogonalFamily_eigenspace_inf_eigenspace hB).comp
    (f := fun c : Module.End.Eigenvalues B × Module.End.Eigenvalues A => (c.1.val, c.2.val))
    (fun _ _ h => Prod.ext (Subtype.ext (congrArg Prod.fst h)) (Subtype.ext (congrArg Prod.snd h)))
explanation: Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.orthogonalFamily_eigenspace_inf_eigenspace` says that for symmetric `A B` over any `RCLike` field the family `i : 𝕜 × 𝕜 ↦ eigenspace A i.2 ⊓ eigenspace B i.1` (with `subtypeₗᵢ`) is an `OrthogonalFamily`. The library's `JointEigenSpace A B c` is by definition `eigenspace A c.2.val ⊓ eigenspace B c.1.val`, so the library's statement is the same family reindexed along the injection `c ↦ (c.1.val, c.2.val)` from `Eigenvalues B × Eigenvalues A` into `ℂ × ℂ`; it follows in one step by `OrthogonalFamily.comp` (the very same device Mathlib uses for the one-operator version `orthogonalFamily_eigenspaces'`), the only side goal being injectivity of that subtype-product map. The library's own proof already applies this Mathlib theorem (after constructing the injective reindexing map `f`), so it is not an independent result.
